findings.title: SourcePattern::matches allocates one Vec<bool> per pattern token per name
findings.claim: `matches` allocates a fresh `next` vector inside the per-token loop and is invoked once per directory child per pattern component during COPY selection, so a pattern of N tokens costs N+1 heap allocations for every candidate filename on a hot path.
findings.suggested_fix: Allocate both buffers once outside the token loop and swap them each iteration (clearing the scratch buffer), so a match costs at most two allocations regardless of token count.

findings.title: Every scute layer is read and SHA-256 hashed at least twice per build
findings.claim: `verify_references` hashes every manifest layer in full (src/cache/resolve.rs:105 -> Cache::copy_verified, src/cache/mod.rs:129-138), then `verify_chain` immediately re-opens and re-hashes the same scute blobs through `CheckedBlob` (src/cache/chain.rs:142-144), and `VerifiedScute::prepare` reads them a third time to emit the verity tree (src/cache/chain/prepared.rs:52), so the largest immutable artifacts in the system are streamed and hashed 2-3 times back to back.

let receipts = cache.verify_references(&image)?;
            let chain = cache.verify_chain(&image)?;
findings.suggested_fix: Have `verify_references` skip the layers that `verify_chain` will authenticate anyway (or have `verify_chain` consume the receipts already produced), so each scute blob is content-hashed exactly once per build.

findings.title: Compressed scutes are fully decompressed twice just to learn their length
findings.claim: `verify_scute` runs a complete zstd decode of a compressed scute into `io::sink()` only to measure the decoded byte count, then reopens the blob and decodes it a second time to compute the verity root, doubling both the read and the decompression cost for every compressed layer.
findings.suggested_fix: When `descriptor.annotations.data_blocks` is present the geometry is already known, so stream once and compute the trailing padding at EOF instead of running a separate measuring pass.

findings.title: Verity hashing reads cache blobs and writes the tree through unbuffered Files
findings.claim: The uncompressed hot path hands a raw `File` straight to `ScuteExtent::format` for both input and hash-tree output (and `DecodedBlob::Plain` is likewise unwrapped, while only the compressed variant gets a `BufReader` at src/cache/chain.rs:204), so every read/write issued by the block-oriented verity formatter becomes its own syscall rather than being batched.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the data source in a `BufReader` and the hash scratch in a `BufWriter` sized to a multiple of the 4096-byte block (e.g. 64 KiB) on this path, as the compressed path already does.

findings.title: COPY re-resolves and re-opens every path prefix once per descendant file
findings.claim: For each descendant entry the destination writer calls `resolve` on the full joined path, which issues an `openat2`+`fstat` per path component from the root (src/copy/destination.rs:111-151), and `leaf` then calls `directory` which re-walks and `mkdirat`/`openat2`s the same prefix again (src/copy/destination.rs:152-180, :242), making a directory copy O(entries x depth) syscalls over directories that were already created and stat'd moments earlier.
findings.suggested_fix: Carry the already-opened parent directory descriptor down the walk (the entries arrive in sorted order, so each new path shares a prefix with the previous one) instead of re-resolving from the root for every entry.

findings.title: descendants() scans the entire captured context and repeats a map lookup per entry
findings.claim: `descendants` iterates every entry in the whole `BTreeMap` context rather than the ordered range under `self.resolved`, and re-evaluates the loop-invariant `self.is_directory()` — itself a `BTreeMap` lookup keyed by `PathBuf` — once per entry, so copying one small subdirectory from a large repository costs a full scan plus one map lookup per repository entry, repeated for every selected source.
findings.suggested_fix: Hoist the `is_directory()` check out of the closure and use `BTreeMap::range` over the `self.resolved` prefix so the walk is proportional to the subtree, not the whole context.

findings.title: Wildcard source selection scans every context key for each candidate path
findings.claim: Each wildcard path component enumerates children by scanning the full key set and comparing `p.parent()`, so the cost is O(candidates x total entries) per component on an ordered map that already supports a prefix range query.
findings.evidence_quote:
for child in self
                            .entries
                            .keys()
                            .filter(|p| p.parent() == Some(actual.as_path()))
findings.suggested_fix: Use `BTreeMap::range` bounded by the `actual` prefix to enumerate direct children instead of filtering the whole key set.

findings.title: Unbounded zstd decode when a scute omits its data-blocks annotation
findings.claim: When `descriptor.annotations.data_blocks` is absent the measuring pass decompresses the layer with no length limit at all, so a compression-bomb scute (zstd is listed as untrusted input) costs unbounded CPU and wall time here, and the measured size is then used to materialize a scratch file of that size in `prepare` (src/cache/chain/prepared.rs:59-83), turning it into workspace exhaustion — this is a denial-of-service vector, not merely a slow path.
findings.evidence_quote: io::copy(&mut source, &mut io::sink())?
findings.suggested_fix: Apply an absolute decoded-size ceiling (e.g. the same `FilesystemSize::LOGICAL_DEVICE_BYTES` bound used elsewhere) to the unannotated branch so no layer can decode without a limit.

findings.title: Command output relay flushes a write syscall per output line
findings.claim: `io::stdout()`/`io::stderr()` are unconditionally line-buffered in Rust (unlike C, this holds even when redirected to a file or pipe), so relaying a verbose command's output costs at least one `write` syscall and one lock acquisition per newline for the whole duration of every RUN step.
findings.suggested_fix: Relay into a block-buffered writer over the inherited stdout/stderr descriptors (flushing at relay completion) rather than through the line-buffered `Stdout`/`Stderr` handles.

findings.title: Named owner lookup resolves, opens and parses /etc/passwd twice
findings.claim: Resolving a named owner calls `account` once for the uid field and again for the gid field, and each call re-resolves the path, re-opens the file, re-reads up to 16 MiB and re-scans every line to find the same record.
findings.evidence_quote:
Some(name) => (
                self.account("/etc/passwd", name, 2)?,
                self.account("/etc/passwd", name, 3)?,
            ),
findings.suggested_fix: Return both fields from a single `account` read of the matching line instead of reading and parsing the database twice.

findings.title: Glob matcher heap-allocates a state vector per token per candidate name
findings.claim: `matches` allocates one `Vec<bool>` up front and another inside the per-token loop, and it is invoked once per candidate child during wildcard selection (src/copy/source.rs:119-121), so matching costs tokens x candidates heap allocations rather than reusing two scratch buffers.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep two reusable buffers (clearing and resizing in place, swapping them each token) so the matcher allocates at most once per call.
